answer: Compute-Credit Ledger. Each agent identity must continuously supply verified compute to the shared pool, and a rising tide of routine workloads consumes that credit over time. An idle or newly minted identity drains its balance and enters a vault of suspended rights, unable to transact until it replenishes. Every outbound action emits a signed usage record that serves as a costly signal, since forging it requires real cycles. An attacker running thousands of sybils must pay sustained compute costs to keep each identity solvent, making mass fabrication economically self-defeating.
